page: Microsoft Azure L80as_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine engineered for high-throughput I/O and large-scale data manipulation. Powered by the AMD EPYC 9V74 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, this instance provisions 80 dedicated vCPUs spanning 40 physical cores with multithreading enabled at a clock speed of up to 3.7 GHz. System memory capacity totals 640.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio. Attached directly to the instance is 19,200 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, designed to deliver high local disk bandwidth without relying exclusively on remote persistent volumes. The instance runs under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization and does not bundle hardware GPUs.

Performance benchmarks confirm robust computational and disk-adjacent capabilities. Multi-core compute tests such as Geekbench (multi-core score of 22,523.0) and PassMark CPU (score of 86,210.97) register in the top 10% tier, aided by modern vector instruction sets including AVX-512 extensions and cryptographic acceleration via VAES and SHA-NI. The instance excels at software compilation (61,006.0 in Geekbench Clang) and multi-threaded decompression (499.47 GB/sec in bzip3). In data store evaluations, the configuration achieves 106.48 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 28,377.64 in PassMark database operations, both placing in the top 25% bracket.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, the L80as_v4 pairs dense dedicated compute with an extensive 19.2 TB local NVMe layer and 640 GB of system memory. Although single-threaded decompression and PassMark overall memory throughput score within the average tier, uncached memory bandwidth sustains 190.57 GB/sec for reads and 117.51 GB/sec for writes. The absence of complimentary public IPv4 addresses requires planned network ingress architecture.

This server type is primarily suited for large relational databases, distributed NoSQL datastores like Apache Cassandra and Redis, real-time analytics engines, big data ETL processing, and high-concurrency static web serving.
